title: Which primes survive a shift of the dyadic sampling grid?
description:
For each real algebraic sampling phase between one and two, the 547/727 and 571/599 races have exactly specified recoverable prime logarithms. At phase 3/2 neither field isolates one prime alone and together they isolate 31 and 47. On the phase interval (97/64,49/32] no prime can be isolated even jointly. For each odd prime a countable dense set of transcendental phases recovers its logarithm using a rational multiple of a single specified reading. The union of all phases recovering a prime by any finite algebraic combination is countable. All claims are unconditional.

Phase classification and arithmetic certificates.
